patchScale.basis: 128 px patches sampled from the scenes, half of them oil-centred

threshold.reason: chosen on the validation split by maximising iou; the full sweep is recorded alongside so the trade-off is visible

baseline.method: despeckled VV, threshold at a calibrated decibel offset below a clean-water reference, morphological opening and a minimum-area filter

train.rule: positives only; the cache holds more oil-bearing patches than the budget

val.rule: positives only; the cache holds more oil-bearing patches than the budget

test.rule: every oil-bearing patch kept; negatives thinned at random to fit

protocol.splitGrouping: train/val/test are assigned by parent Sentinel-1 acquisition, so no crop of one product appears in more than one split
protocol.normalisationSource: training split patches only, invalid pixels excluded

thresholdSelection.reason: chosen on the validation split by maximising iou; the full sweep is recorded alongside so the trade-off is visible

protocol.invalidPixels: excluded from the loss and from every reported metric

limitations: Every supplied scene contains labelled oil, so these figures measure delineation quality on scenes already known to contain a slick; they are not a false-alarm rate on clean sea.
The dataset contains no labelled look-alikes (algal blooms, low-wind zones, rain cells, ship wakes), so the model's ability to reject them is untested and unquantified here.
Metrics are computed on 128 px patches sampled from the scenes rather than on whole 2048 px scenes, so they do not include errors that only appear at scene scale.
The reference masks are the supplied labels; their own accuracy is unknown and is treated as ground truth throughout.

sceneScale.basis: Whole-scene evaluation at 2048x2048. The patch metrics in metrics.json are measured on 128 px crops sampled around labelled oil and therefore do not include the false positives that only appear at scene scale.
sceneScale.thresholdSelection: chosen on the validation scenes by mean per-scene IoU, then applied unchanged to the test scenes
limitations: Every supplied scene contains labelled oil, so these figures still measure delineation on scenes known to contain a slick and are not a false-alarm rate on clean sea.
Scene-scale IoU is markedly lower than patch-scale IoU because the patch sampler never visited most of each frame; the scene figure is the one that reflects operating on a full acquisition.
The reference masks are the supplied labels and are treated as ground truth; their own accuracy is unknown.

lookAlike.question: Given a dark region in a SAR scene, is it oil or a look-alike? Every other metric in this project assumes the answer is already oil.

features.name: darknessZ
features.label: darkness against local water
features.rationale: oil damps the short capillary waves the radar sees, so a film sits several standard deviations below the water around it; a low-wind patch is shallower because the water is only slightly smoother, not covered

features.name: darknessP10Z
features.label: darkness of the darkest tenth
features.rationale: a mean can be dragged down by a few very dark pixels, so the tenth percentile asks whether the whole region is dark or only part of it

features.name: textureRatio
features.label: interior roughness
features.rationale: a damped surface is smoother than the sea around it, so its pixel spread is narrower; wind shadows and blooms stay as speckled as open water

features.name: edgeSharpness
features.label: edge definition
features.rationale: a film has a physical boundary and the backscatter steps across it; a low-wind zone fades, so its edge gradient is no stronger than the ambient texture

features.name: compactness
features.label: compactness
features.rationale: spills are drawn out by wind and current into ragged forms; a compact blob is more consistent with a wind cell or a bloom patch

features.name: solidity
features.label: solidity
features.rationale: a slick feathers at its edges and leaves gaps inside its hull; a smooth convex region is a weaker candidate

features.name: elongation
features.label: elongation
features.rationale: a discharge from a moving vessel is linear, and wind stretches any film along its axis, so elongation argues for oil -- though a ship wake is linear too, which is why this feature is never decisive on its own

screen.calibration: fitted on 11623 dark regions (930 over labelled oil, 10693 not)

trainedOn.labelRule: a dark region counts as oil when the supplied reference mask covers >= 50% of it and as not-oil when it covers <= 5%; the rest are dropped rather than guessed at
trainedOn.proposerNote: the proposer is the same code that runs on the look-alike set and is given no reference mask; its recall of the labelled oil is reported so a high screening score cannot hide a proposer that simply missed the slick

limitations: The look-alike labels in the same-domain half are the absence of oil in the supplied reference mask, not a positive identification of a phenomenon. A dark region the mask does not cover may be low wind, a wake, an unlabelled slick, or a labelling error.

The screen decides between oil and a look-alike for a region that has already been proposed. It cannot recover a slick the proposer never found, and its sensitivity is therefore conditional on the proposer, not on the sea.

A region the screen calls uncertain stays in the case. That is deliberate for a response tool -- suppressing an unsure detection would trade a measured false positive for an unmeasured missed spill -- but it means the rejection rate is the rate of outright rejections and not one minus the acceptance rate.

The screen was fitted on 270 parent products; a linear model over seven features on that many independent sites is a screen, not a classifier of phenomena, and it deliberately never names which look-alike it thinks it is looking at.

The look-alike patches are 8-bit JPEG at about 20 m/pixel from a different sea. They are resampled to this project's ground sampling before scoring and every model feature is a ratio of same-unit quantities, so the comparison is defensible -- but the unpublished greyscale stretch remains an untested assumption behind the invariance claim.

126 of 2290 look-alike patches produced no dark region at all, so the proposer -- not the screen -- is what rejected them. They are counted in the patch rate and absent from the region rate, which is why both are reported.

The detector's false-alarm rate is indicative, not a published figure. An 8-bit JPEG cannot be turned back into calibrated decibels and the archive is single-channel, so the second polarisation is synthesised from the first and is perfectly correlated with it. Two mappings are reported precisely because one number would overstate what the data supports.
